properties.article_text_excerpt: A police car leaving RAF Molesworth after the two men were arrested. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters View image in fullscreen A police car leaving RAF Molesworth after the two men were arrested. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters UK news Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by US military Men aged 32 and 36 detained on suspicion of trespass, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor Thu 8 Oct 2026 17.27 EDT First published on Thu 8 Oct 2026 11.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two Latvian men were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they were discovered inside the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a Cambridgeshire base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations. The men, 32 and 36, were picked up at 2am inside the base, in an investigation that began four hours earlier when military police discovered an abandoned vehicle outside the facility. Military police, helped by officers from Cambridgeshire police, discovered a small hole in the perimeter fence before finding and arresting the men, initially on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and causing criminal damage. properties.article_text_excerpt: Romania's head of state, Nicusor Dan, on Monday signed a law aimed at reducing the country's bear population, a bill he had previously challenged on constitutional grounds and sent back to parliament for reconsideration.The legislation, which was re-adopted by the Chamber of Deputies on 16 September, allows the preventive shooting of 859 brown bears this year. A further 110 protected large wild animals may be hunted as an intervention measure if they pose a threat to human life.In recent years it has become common in Romania for bears to appear in inhabited areas, and the number of bear attacks has risen sharply, with more and more fatal incidents.According to the results of an earlier survey mapping the brown bear population, Romania is home to Europe's largest bear population and the greatest genetic diversity among bear species.The study put the number of individuals at between 10,600 and 12,700.Last week, Covasna County prefect Ráduly István warned that, because of the limited time available, it would be impossible to meet this year's quota. properties.article_text_excerpt: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung said on Friday that Seoul would take "further measures" if Ukraine refuses to publicly apologise over what he called its unilateral disclosure of North Korean POWs being sent to South Korea.Seoul has taken a hard stance on Ukraine disclosing the transfer of two soldiers captured fighting for Russia, warning that their families could be targeted by Pyongyang.North Korea is known to retaliate against defectors and their families.Both POWs are identifiable as they had been photographed by South Korean media before their arrival to the South.The POWs were captured by Ukrainian forces early last year after being deployed alongside thousands of North Korean troops to support Russia's war against Ukraine, in exchange for economic and military assistance to Pyongyang.Hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed last week the transfer in remarks at the United Nations, Lee expressed his dismay, with Seoul claiming confidentiality was key to protecting the POWs' relatives.Seoul later demanded an official apology from Ukraine, saying that both sides had reached a "clear understanding" during consultations to keep the transfer confidential."
